    {"name": "premium_class_value_perception", "analytical_usefulness": 0.75, "source_groundedness": 0.85, "rationale": "Useful for premium-cabin ROI analysis.     {"name": "passenger_class_factor", "analytical_usefulness": 0.55, "source_groundedness": 0.55, "rationale": "Class is analytically relevant but largely redundant with the existing original 'Class' column. Grounding is questionable: samples 1 and 2 labeled 'business' with no class stated in the source text, an unsupported specific.", "hallucination_observed": true}
  ],
  "analytical_usefulness": 0.78,
  "source_groundedness": 0.72,
  "rationale": "The added columns give genuine new analytical axes (complaint drivers, seat/food/crew qualitative reads, operational issues, premium value) that are well aligned to the MD's route/service optimisation goal, and most values are sound readings of the source. Weaknesses: several columns lack a NULL/unknown bucket (service_delivery_consistency, passenger_class_factor) or assign confident specifics on rows where the text is silent (ground_staff 'adequate_standard', class 'business'), and some labels flatten or contradict clear praise (crew 'polite_but_detached' from 'staff excellent'). passenger_class_factor is also largely redundant with the original Class column. Overall useful but with recurring unwarranted-specificity grounding issues."
